Thanks Olivia — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a concise scenario workbook and a one-page MAP draft you can include in approvals. High-level summary below; details are in SLA-pricing-model-v3.xlsx and MAP-draft-CirrusHealth.pdf attached.

Proposed pilot structure (30 days):
- Uptime bands: >=99.95% (Platinum), 99.5–99.95% (Gold), <99.5% (Silver pilot exception)
- Response windows: Sev1 initial response 15 minutes (Platinum), 30 minutes (Gold), 60 minutes (Silver)
- Pilot credit mechanics: if monthly uptime <99.5% during pilot, we apply a capped credit equal to 10% of the pilot month fee up to a ceiling of $20k. Credits do not compound across multiple breaches during pilot.
- Escalation coverage: 24/7 triage for Sev1 for Platinum & Gold during pilot; dedicated escalation SLA holder assigned to CirrusHealth for the pilot window.

Pricing impact: to make the pilot low-friction we offer a 12% pilot discount on committed capacity plus the capped credit above. The workbook shows blended monthly costs across three capacity scenarios (10k, 25k, 50k tokens/day).

Next steps I suggest: 1) you confirm the pilot ceiling and response windows, 2) we circulate the MAP draft to procurement, 3) if OK we send a short DocuSign for an experimental pilot addendum.

If helpful, Karthik can run a variant with lower cap/larger credit and show the tradeoffs.

Cheers,

Olivia — adding a couple of concession options we can use if procurement pushes back on the 10%/20k cap:

Option A (conservative): 8% pilot discount, credit = 8% of pilot month fee up to $12.5k. No change to response windows.
Option B (balanced): 10% pilot discount, credit = 12% of pilot month fee up to $30k, but credits tier per breach (first breach capped at 8k, subsequent breaches up to remaining cap).
Option C (operational): Keep 12% pilot discount, credit stays at 10% up to $20k but require weekly operational sync and an ops playbook sign-off to limit unknowns.

Attached are quick sensitivity tabs in the workbook showing TCV impact and a sample runbook excerpt for Option C. If Cirrus prefers a firm cap we should aim for Option A or C.

Olivia — looping in one more point from an ops/exec perspective. We want to standardize the escalation roster for pilots so both sides know who owns each boundary. Proposal: during the 30-day pilot we provide a named escalation lead plus a backup; for extended contracts the named lead becomes part of the managed oncall rota.

Additionally, because Cirrus is in regulated healthcare, we will add an explicit non-compounding clause for pilot credits and a single remediation pathway (credit only; no refunds). That keeps liability predictable.

I'll approve Option C for the pilot provided procurement accepts the playbook and the cap of $20k. If procurement insists on a higher ceiling, we can switch to a staged credit that reduces after week two.
